questions.stem: This question tests algorithms and programming errors.

parts.answer: An algorithm is a finite sequence of precise steps that solves a problem. Pseudocode is a structured English-like description of an algorithm.
parts.solution: Award 1 mark for each correct definition.
parts.label: a

parts.text: Explain THREE types of programming errors and give one example of each.
parts.answer: Syntax error: missing semicolon. Runtime error: division by zero. Logic error: using < instead of <= in a condition.
parts.solution: Award 0.5 mark for each type and 0.5 mark for a valid example.
parts.label: b

questions.stem: A concert charges the ticket prices shown in Table 1. A negative age is invalid.

parts.text: Draw a flowchart for the ticket price selection.
parts.answer: Start -> read age -> if age < 0 display invalid; else if age <= 12 price = 15; else if age <= 17 price = 25; else price = 40 -> display price -> end.
parts.solution: Award marks for validation, all ranges, output and flow.
parts.label: a

parts.text: Write pseudocode and a complete C++ program for the ticket price selection.
parts.answer: Use if/else if with the three ranges and an invalid-age branch.
parts.solution: Award marks for validation, range conditions, assignment and output.
parts.label: b

questions.stem: This question tests type conversion and constants.

parts.text: Explain the difference between implicit and explicit type conversion, and give one C++ example of each.
parts.answer: Implicit conversion is automatic (int to double); explicit conversion uses a cast such as double(total) or static_cast<double>(total).
parts.solution: Award marks for both definitions and valid examples.
parts.label: a

parts.text: Write a C++ program segment that calculates the average of three integer marks as a double and displays it to two decimal places.
parts.answer: double average = (m1 + m2 + m3) / 3.0; cout << fixed << setprecision(2) << average;
parts.solution: Award marks for floating-point division, fixed/setprecision and output.
parts.label: b

parts.text: Rewrite the segment using a do...while loop that sums only values greater than 5.
parts.answer: int i=0,s=0; do { if(a[i]>5) s+=a[i]; i++; } while(i<5); cout<<s;

questions.stem: A sports club records the sport names and medal counts in Table 1.

parts.text: Declare two parallel arrays for the five sports in Table 1 and initialise them with those values.

parts.text: Write a program segment to display each sport with its medals, then calculate the total and average medals.
parts.answer: Loop i=0..4 to display sports[i] and medals[i], accumulate total, average = double(total)/5.
